newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines limits banks' exposure to property.
newsitem.headline: Philippines limits banks' exposure to property.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank has set a 20 percent limit on loan exposure of banks to the real estate sector, Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday.
Singson said each bank could only lend up to a maximum of 20 percent of its loan portfolio to real estate builders and homeowners.
"Banks which currently overshoot the 20 pecent ceiling have been given one year to comply," he said in a statement.
This is the first time the Central Bank has set such a limit.
Data from end-1996 showed the banking industry has lent about 11 percent of its loanable funds to the property sector.
Data on the property loan exposures of individual banks was not available.
Singson said the Monetary Board had also approved a lowering of the loan value to 60 percent from the previous 70 percent of a property's appraised value.
The appraised value is 80 percent of the prevailing market value.
Central Bank deputy governor Alberto Reyes, in an earlier interview, said the lower loan value would serve as a safeguard for banks in case property prices collapsed.
The measures are "designed to prevent banks from overlending to the real estate sector that could undermine the country's financial system," Singson added.
Singson sought to allay fears over the quality of property loans Philippine banks were exposed to.
Of the 78.8 billion pesos worth of real estate loans as of last December, only 1.15 percent had been found to be past due.
"This ratio compares well against the 7.73 percent non-performing loans registered by Thailand's commercial banks in the first half of 1996," he added.
Out of the total exposure, 70.3 percent were fully secured loans while the remaining were extended to high net-worth individuals and companies enjoying good credit ratings.
The Philippine markets have been hounded by fears of a repeat of the Thailand experience where land prices crashed leading to rising bad debts.
